exposure: Inflammatory bowel diseases (Ulcerative Colitis, Crohn's disease)
Serum cytokine levels (IL-6, IL-22, IL-21, IFN-g)
outcome: IBD disease activity (biochemical: C-reactive protein [CRP], fecal calprotectin [FCP]; clinical activities)
cohort: The study included 11 healthy pregnant women and 76 pregnant women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD).
finding: Elevated T1 (first trimester) serum cytokine levels of IL-22 (>0.624 pg/mL) and IL-6 (>0.648 pg/mL) were associated with worse IBD disease activity throughout pregnancy in women with UC and CD, respectively.
